XXXII, 14</cite>) <he>אלו ס׳ שלהם</he> that means their (the Roman) senators (sent to the provinces); (<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 317">Sifré Deut. 317</cite> <cite ref="O01261"><he>סנקנירקים</he></cite>, Var. <cite ref="O01261"><he>סנקירקים</he></cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 944">Yalk. ib. 944</cite> <he>סרקני דקין</he>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2:12">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵈ</cite> <he>חילף את כל ס׳ שלו</he> he changed all his councilors; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 11:5:7">Y. Snh. XI, 30ᶜ</cite> top (some ed. <cite ref="O01262"><he>סנקליטון</he></cite>, v. infra).

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 13:5">Lev. R. s. 13</cite> <he>גחין ואמר לסִנְקְלִיטָין וכ׳</he> he bent down and said to his assessors, these three things (for which I put to death three persons) did I do in one night; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 80:6">Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXX</cite> <he>לסִנְקְלִיט שלו</he> (sing.; ed. Bub. <cite ref="O01260"><he>סנקוטס</he></cite>, oth. ed. <he>טוקלוס</he>, <cite ref="O01262"><he>סנקלוס</he></cite>; corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 8:3">Gen. R. s. 8</cite> <he>מלך שהיו לו שני ס׳ וכ׳</he> a king that had two counselors, without whose consent he did nothing; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 13:3">Yalk. ib. 13</cite>; a. fr.
